properties.rationale: Both carry project_code; a project has one plan line per fiscal year and vintage.
A project has one working forecast per forecast date.
Ledger lines carry the project code. Lines without one stay unallocated rather than being attributed.
Order lines name the project they commit.
Every approval and budget revision is raised against one project.
A contract delivers one project; a project can have several contracts.
Change orders are numbered within their contract.
Orders release against a contract; stand-alone orders carry no contract.
Each project belongs to one utility.
A project can be claimed in more than one docket.
The in-service file has one row per project; 260 rows match no project and are kept as unmatched.
Assets placed in service carry the project they came from.
One depreciation row per asset per month.
Deductions and additions are kept per utility.
A catalogue item has one framework price while the agreement is valid; an off-framework line still matches its item.

story_group.story: Northline Water Group runs four regulated water utilities (Ardenia, Belmara, Corvale and Dunmoor), each under its own state commission, plus a shared services division. The capital program holds 4,500 projects, 3,768 of them approved, with $8.27B of approved budget; a project is keyed by project_code (C23B225_690 for a discrete project, CZZF50229_623 for a blanket). The approved budget lives in the EPBCS plan by fiscal year and vintage (Working, Jan Calendarization, MTP); the working forecast is a snapshot per forecast date with actuals to date, committed, uncommitted and contingency held separately, and forecasts land on the 15th of each month. Posted actuals come from the PeopleSoft ledger; ledger lines with no project code stay unallocated. Order lines are commitments, and open commitment is ordered minus received minus cancelled. A change to an approved budget goes through a WIN budget revision with an approval level; a large project more than 10% over its approved budget needs one. Contracts are changed by change orders, and a requested change order is not approved budget. Projects claimed in a rate case carry the docket, the test year end and the rate base; the expected in-service date comes from the governed in-service upload, which does not cover every project. Primavera P6 is not connected, so milestones and critical path are not in this graph.

grain.Approved_Budgets: one project x fiscal year x plan vintage
grain.In_Service_Dates: one row per project in the file
grain.Rate_Base_Components: one utility x component x period

uncertainties: epbcs.forecast holds several rounds per month for projects a project office reloaded; the latest forecast_date is taken as the working forecast.
63 Lakeshore projects have no forecast after 15 June (cost tool cut-over); their forecast is stale, not missing.
upload.inservice names 260 project codes that do not exist in pmo.project.
pmo.change_order.cost_impact_usd is the requested value until co_status is Approved.
gl.project_costing_line.project_code is null on 0.4% of lines (unallocated).
Milestones and float are not available: Primavera P6 is not connected.

type_links.reason: Documents name projects by the same project code the project master is keyed on.
Documents name the utilities exactly as pmo.utility does.
Contract numbers in documents match pmo.contract keys.
Change order numbers match pmo.change_order within their contract.
WIN numbers in documents and mail match the WIN register.
A docket in a document is the docket the claims are filed under, not a claim row itself.
The commission regulates the utility; pmo.utility carries it as an attribute.
Amounts in documents may be budgets, forecasts or change order values; only the basis tells which.
A forecast quoted in a deck or a mail is a statement; the forecast table is the record.
Change order values are printed in the change order documents.
Percentages in documents are variances computed at a date; they are not stored.
People are named as project managers; personal data, masked for analysts.
A date in a mail is a statement until the in-service file carries it.
Filing and test year dates bound a claim.
The committee and Level 03 approve revisions.
Regions and plant names locate projects; no GIS to confirm geometry.
Contractors are parties to contracts.
Claims are lined per project.
Forecasts are per project.
A person who raised a revision is not the revision.
A change order is not an approved budget line; it needs a WIN revision.
